# The ways we are trying to build it

## Approach one, composable Turing models

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
- Three kinds of part. A prior model, an infection model, an observation
  model
- Each part is a plain struct with one method of `as_turing_model`
- Joint inference and the rest of the Turing toolchain come with it
- So do one PPL's design decisions. Nested submodel dispatch is slow, and
  `condition` assumes fixed-length data

::: {.attribution}
Code from
[epiaware.org/approaches/composable-turing-models.html][cturing], read
2026-08-12, blank lines and comments removed to fit ·
[ComposableTuringIDModels.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/ComposableTuringIDModels.jl).
:::
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
```julia
using ComposableTuringIDModels, Distributions, Turing
data = IDData(gen_distribution = Gamma(1.4, 1 / 0.38))
model = IDModel(
    Renewal(data;
        rt = AR(; ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(
            std_prior = HalfNormal(0.1))),
        initialisation_prior = Normal(log(1.0), 1.0)),
    LatentDelay(
        Ascertainment(NegativeBinomialError(),
            Intercept(Normal(log(0.4), 0.1))),
        truncated(Normal(5.0, 2.0), 0.0, Inf)))
chain = sample(as_turing_model(model, cases, length(cases)),
               NUTS(), MCMCThreads(), 1_000, 2)
```
:::
::::

## Approach two, composed distributions

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
- Every leaf is an ordinary `Distributions.jl` distribution, and so is the
  tree they compose into
- `rand` simulates a case and `logpdf` scores one, with no PPL involved
- The tree is data you can read and edit, a parameter table and a nested
  prior
- It has no account of a time series or a latent trajectory, and it needs
  its own fitting layer

::: {.attribution}
Code from [epiaware.org/approaches/composed-distributions.html][cdists],
read 2026-08-12, blank lines, comments and the three inspection calls
removed to fit ·
[ComposedDistributions.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/ComposedDistributions.jl)
and `DistributionsInference.jl`.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
```julia
using ComposedDistributions, Distributions
tree = @uncertain compose((
    clinical = sequential(
        :onset_admit => Gamma(Normal(1.2, 0.2), 3.0),
        :admit_resolve => resolve(
            :death => (Gamma(2.0, 3.5), 0.3),
            :discharge => (Gamma(1.0, 8.0), 0.7))),
    surveillance = sequential(
        :onset_notif => Gamma(0.7, 20.0),
        :notif_compete => compete(
            :confirmed => Gamma(2.0, 1.0),
            :lost => Gamma(5.0, 0.5))),))
case = rand(tree); logpdf(tree, case)
```
:::
::::

## Lowering into SciML, and writing the model by hand

- `lower` turns a delay distribution into a compartmental generator, and
  four backends share the same lowering. Catalyst, SciMLBase, JumpProcesses
  and AlgebraicPetri
- Composing dynamical systems is not the same problem as composing
  probability models, so inference has to be supplied separately
- A model written by hand is what everyone does now, and the baseline the
  other three have to beat
- We are running all of them because I cannot tell you which is right

::: {.callout-note}
A bet. The three we are building take the same `Distributions.jl` objects
and the same gradients.
:::

::: {.attribution}
[LoweredDistributions.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/LoweredDistributions.jl)
README, read 2026-08-10 · alternatives we are not running, including
AlgebraicJulia, Gen.jl, NumPyro and ModelingToolkit.jl, are in the
composable modelling paper, in preparation.
